abstract: Zero-shot voice cloning typically emphasizes preserving the timbre and prosodic characteristics of a reference speaker. However, in real-world use, speech should adapt its delivery to the target text rather than remain tied to a fixed speaking style. In this work, we formulate this problem as text-adaptive prosody synthesis for zero-shot voice cloning and study how post-training can endow a cloning model with this capability. We develop a three-stage framework. First, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) provides a cold start by aligning the model with text-appropriate expressive speech. Second, Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) jointly optimizes prosodic expressiveness, acoustic quality, intelligibility, and speaker similarity. Finally, context-conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) enables self-improvement by transferring expressive behavior from strong-reference to weak-reference conditions. On Qwen3-TTS, our framework improves Emotion from 18.5 to 81.2 and Paralinguistics from 38.4 to 73.9. Extensive ablations validate the role of each stage.

oneSentenceThesis: 本文把零样本克隆从模仿参考韵律改为按目标文本生成合适韵律，用偏好数据冷启动、多目标策略优化和弱参考自蒸馏依次推进，在 Qwen3-TTS 上把表情与副语言得分大幅提高，但说话人相似度有所下降。
originalTitle: Rethinking Post-Training for Expressive Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
readerTitle: 让克隆的声音按文本要求去表达：三段式后训练怎么做
